questions.question: A gastroenterologist is performing an esophagoscopy in a patient with severe acid reflux. At which level will he encounter its diaphragmatic constriction?

suspectLines.text: The esophageal hiatus is at the T10 vertebral level and forms the diaphragmatic constriction of the esophagus. The source lists contents of the hiatus as the esophagus, vagal trunks, gastric nerves, esophageal branches of the left gastric vessels and some lymphatics. It also gives the normal esophageal constrictions measured from the upper incisors: cricopharyngeus at 15 cm, aortic arch at 22.5 cm, left bronchus at 27.5 cm and diaphragmatic opening at 37.5 cm.
